status: Uncalibrated, source-documented assumptions; congestion is an assumed scenario, not recorded or estimated historical traffic
capacity_note: K = directional lanes x saturation flow x g/C. 1,900 veh/h/lane is an assumed base saturation flow (not validated locally); g/C = 0.5 is assumed at approaches to a mapped signal, 1 elsewhere. Unsignalized use is a rough proxy, not a validated link-capacity model. Uncertainty: lanes often fall back to road-type defaults and signal timings are unmeasured.
traffic_note: Assumed congestion scenario, not observed, counted or independently estimated traffic: a seeded, assumed hourly demand-to-capacity index per road segment (hourly profile x road-type factor x weekend factor x repeatable city, area and road variation) passed through the BPR function. Preprocessed into data/processed/temporal/traffic_hourly.csv, one row per segment per hour.
weather_note: Weather severity a per road = assumed severity of the hourly weather category; it is kept separate from mapped flood exposure. Severities and travel-time multipliers are assumptions, not calibrated. Category from hourly provider precipitation: Weatherstack ws_precip_mm is a 1-hour accumulation in mm (verified: the 24 hourly values sum to the daily total). heavy_rain: >= 7.5 mm/h; rain: > 0 mm/h; clear: 0 mm/h. When precipitation is missing, the description decides ('heavy rain'/'torrential' -> heavy_rain; 'rain'/'drizzle'/'thunder' -> rain) and the record is flagged; when both are missing the observation is missing and the request fails instead of assuming clear.

traffic_variation.note: Repeatable variation per road segment: daily (per city), three-hour (per ~1.1 km area, shared by neighbouring roads), static (per road) and three-hour (per road). Uncalibrated scenario coefficients, not measurements.

road_class_severity.definition: p_k = 1 - median free-flow speed of class k / largest class median, over development roads; a stated preference for faster road classes, not a published penalty.

flood_class_severity.note: NOAH five-year hazard classes 1-3 are mapped susceptibility, not current inundation or road closure. Overlapping polygons resolve to the highest class.

time_profile_note: Time-profile severity h per road group (city x road type), day category (weekday/weekend) and local hour = mean congestion of the group's roads over development dates only. Fallbacks: road type over all cities, then all roads. The clock hour itself is never a penalty.
